name: John Heywood
bio: John Heywood (c. 1497 - c. 1580) was a court musician and writer of interludes under Henry VIII and Mary I. He played the virginals at court and was a favourite of both monarchs, and his short comic plays, among them The Four PP and The Play of the Weather, were staged in the 1520s and 1530s.

He also made a large collection of English proverbs and published epigrams in verse. A firm Catholic, he left England after Elizabeth I came to the throne and lived in exile at Malines (Mechelen) in the Low Countries, where he died about 1580.
